facts.text: In software-in-the-loop (SIL), the target algorithms and software are real, usually compiled for a host PC rather than the final controller.
facts.quote: the target algorithms and software, usually compiled for a host PC rather than the final controller.

facts.text: Software-in-the-loop (SIL) needs a scenario or world model, an environment simulation with ideal, phenomenological or physics-based sensor models or semantic inputs, a machine dynamics model including braking, articulation and load, and a test oracle.
facts.quote: a scenario or world model, an environment simulation with sensor models (ideal, phenomenological or physics-based) or semantic inputs, a machine dynamics model that includes braking, articulation and load, and a test oracle.

facts.text: Software-in-the-loop (SIL) control tests are usually closed-loop.

Software-in-the-loop (SIL) can establish logic correctness, timing in simulated time, boundary exploration, requirements tests, very high-volume regression, and coverage of large scenario sets in closed loop, where the machine reacts and the scene evolves.
facts.quote: logic correctness, timing in simulated time, boundary exploration, requirements tests, very high-volume regression, and coverage of large scenario sets in closed loop (the machine reacts and the scene evolves).

facts.text: Software-in-the-loop (SIL) is recommended for parametrically sweeping the 100+ site types and 10+ scenarios.
facts.quote: It is the right tool for sweeping the 100+ site types and 10+ scenarios parametrically.

facts.text: Software-in-the-loop (SIL) cannot prove real sensor physics in dust, snow or glare unless the sensor models are validated.
facts.quote: real sensor physics in dust, snow or glare unless the sensor models are validated

facts.text: Software-in-the-loop (SIL) cannot prove timing, processor and I/O faults of the final ECU.
facts.quote: timing, processor and I/O faults of the final ECU

facts.text: Software-in-the-loop (SIL) cannot prove actual brake hardware.
facts.quote: **Cannot prove:** real sensor physics in dust, snow or glare unless the sensor models are validated; timing, processor and I/O faults of the final ECU; actual brake hardware.

facts.text: Software-in-the-loop (SIL) is only as credible as its models.
facts.quote: It is only as credible as its models.
